parse.title: Catharsis
parse.wikitext:
<onlyinclude>
'''Catharsis''' (from the Greek ''katharsis'') is precisely defined as a ''cleansing'', with no substantial consensus in regards to its exact meaning.<ref name=":1">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Solbakk, J. H.)) | journal=Medicine, Health Care and Philosophy | title=‘Catharsis and moral therapy II: An Aristotelian account’ | volume=9 | issue=2 | pages=141–153 | date= July 2006 | url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s11019-005-8319-1 | doi=10.1007/s11019-005-8319-1}}</ref> Generally, this effect is a form of emotional insight.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Roseman, L.)), ((Nutt, D. J.)), ((Carhart-Harris, R. L.)) | journal=Frontiers in Pharmacology | title=Quality of Acute Psychedelic Experience Predicts Therapeutic Efficacy of Psilocybin for Treatment-Resistant Depression | volume=8 | date= 2018 | url=https://www.frontiersin.org/article/10.3389/fphar.2017.00974 | issn=1663-9812}}
</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Tesser, A.)), ((Leone, C.)), ((Clary, E. G.)) | journal=Cognitive Therapy and Research | title=Affect control: Process Constraints versus Catharsis | volume=2 | issue=3 | pages=265–274 | date= September 1978 | url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF01185788 | issn=0147-5916 | doi=10.1007/BF01185788}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Winkelman, M.)) | journal=Complementary health practice review | title=Psychointegrators: Multidisciplinary Perspectives on the Therapeutic Effects of Hallucinogens | volume=6 | issue=3 | pages=219–237 | date= July 2001 | url=http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/153321010100600304 | issn=1533-2101 | doi=10.1177/153321010100600304}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Kaelen, M.)), ((Barrett, F. S.)), ((Roseman, L.)), ((Lorenz, R.)), ((Family, N.)), ((Bolstridge, M.)), ((Curran, H. V.)), ((Feilding, A.)), ((Nutt, D. J.)), ((Carhart-Harris, R. L.)) | journal=Psychopharmacology | title=LSD enhances the emotional response to music | volume=232 | issue=19 | pages=3607–3614 | date= October 2015 | url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s00213-015-4014-y | issn=0033-3158 | doi=10.1007/s00213-015-4014-y}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Gasser, P.)), ((Kirchner, K.)), ((Passie, T.)) | journal=Journal of Psychopharmacology | title=LSD-assisted psychotherapy for anxiety associated with a life-threatening disease: A qualitative study of acute and sustained subjective effects | volume=29 | issue=1 | pages=57–68 | date= January 2015 | url=http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0269881114555249 | issn=0269-8811 | doi=10.1177/0269881114555249}}</ref> The process typically starts off being difficult to fully face and is sometimes accompanied by physically intense sensations which typically lead into pronounced [[Emotion intensification|emotion intensification]], deep [[introspection]], and an [[analysis enhancement|analysis]] of one's character and past events.<ref name="BelserAgin-Liebes2017">{{cite journal|last1=Belser|first1=Alexander B.|last2=Agin-Liebes|first2=Gabrielle|last3=Swift|first3=T. Cody|last4=Terrana|first4=Sara|last5=Devenot|first5=Neşe|last6=Friedman|first6=Harris L.|last7=Guss|first7=Jeffrey|last8=Bossis|first8=Anthony|last9=Ross|first9=Stephen|title=Patient Experiences of Psilocybin-Assisted Psychotherapy: An Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis|journal=Journal of Humanistic Psychology|volume=57|issue=4|year=2017|pages=354–388|issn=0022-1678|doi=10.1177/0022167817706884}}</ref> During this experience many people describe reliving traumatic events, witnessing painful memories, having enhanced mental imagery, reliving of past experiences, painful feelings in general, and a release of previously repressed emotions.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4" /><ref name="BelserAgin-Liebes2017" /> This process of integrating manifestations of conflicts and traumas into long-term stable memories is often described as feeling very natural.  

This effect can be helpful in aiding an individual overcome conditions such as [[Addiction suppression|addiction]],<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Bogenschutz, M. P.)), ((Johnson, M. W.)) | journal=Progress in Neuro-Psychopharmacology and Biological Psychiatry | title=Classic hallucinogens in the treatment of addictions | volume=64 | pages=250–258 | date= January 2016 | url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0278584615000512 | issn=02785846 | doi=10.1016/j.pnpbp.2015.03.002}}</ref> post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), and other personal afflictions relating to suffered past traumas.<ref name=":5">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Garcia-Romeu, A.)), ((Kersgaard, B.)), ((Addy, P. H.)) | journal=Experimental and Clinical Psychopharmacology | title=Clinical applications of hallucinogens: A review. | volume=24 | issue=4 | pages=229–268 | date= August 2016 | url=http://doi.apa.org/getdoi.cfm?doi=10.1037/pha0000084 | issn=1936-2293 | doi=10.1037/pha0000084}}</ref> After this experience is over, most users report feelings of increased life satisfaction, [[rejuvenation]], and [[Spirituality intensification|spirituality intensification]] which may last days, weeks, or even years after the event is over.<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Carbonaro, T. M.)), ((Bradstreet, M. P.)), ((Barrett, F. S.)), ((MacLean, K. A.)), ((Jesse, R.)), ((Johnson, M. W.)), ((Griffiths, R. R.)) | journal=Journal of Psychopharmacology | title=Survey study of challenging experiences after ingesting psilocybin mushrooms: Acute and enduring positive and negative consequences | volume=30 | issue=12 | pages=1268–1278 | date= December 2016 | url=http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0269881116662634 | issn=0269-8811 | doi=10.1177/0269881116662634}}</ref>

Catharsis is most commonly induced in [[Set and setting|therapeutic settings]] under the influence of [[dosage#common|moderate]] [[dosage|dosages]] of [[psychedelic]] compounds, such as [[LSD]], [[psilocybin]], and [[mescaline]].<ref name=":5" /><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Winkelman, M.)) | journal=Anthropology of Consciousness | title=Therapeutic Effects of Hallucinogens | volume=2 | issue=3–4 | pages=15–19 | date= September 1991 | url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1525/ac.1991.2.3-4.15 | issn=1053-4202 | doi=10.1525/ac.1991.2.3-4.15}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Hartogsohn, I.)) | journal=Frontiers in Neuroscience | title=The Meaning-Enhancing Properties of Psychedelics and Their Mediator Role in Psychedelic Therapy, Spirituality, and Creativity | volume=12 | date= 2018 | url=https://www.frontiersin.org/article/10.3389/fnins.2018.00129 | issn=1662-453X}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Wolfson, P. E.)) | journal=International Journal of Transpersonal Studies | title=Psychedelic Experiential Pharmacology: Pioneering Clinical Explorations with Salvador Roquet (How I Came to All of This: Ketamine, Admixtures and Adjuvants, Don Juan and Carlos Castaneda Too): An Interview with Richard Yensen | volume=33 | issue=2 | pages=160–174 | date=1 July 2014 | url=https://digitalcommons.ciis.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1026&context=ijts-transpersonalstudies | issn=13210122 | doi=10.24972/ijts.2014.33.2.160}}</ref><ref name=":7">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Kolp, E.)), ((Friedman, H. L.)), ((Krupitsky, E.)), ((Jansen, K.)), ((Sylvester, M.)), ((Young, M. S.)), ((Kolp, A.)) | journal=International Journal of Transpersonal Studies | title=Ketamine Psychedelic Psychotherapy: Focus on its Pharmacology, Phenomenology, and Clinical Applications | volume=33 | issue=2 | pages=84–140 | date=1 July 2014 | url=https://digitalcommons.ciis.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1023&context=ijts-transpersonalstudies | issn=13210122 | doi=10.24972/ijts.2014.33.2.84}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Gasser, P.)), ((Holstein, D.)), ((Michel, Y.)), ((Doblin, R.)), ((Yazar-Klosinski, B.)), ((Passie, T.)), ((Brenneisen, R.)) | journal=Journal of Nervous & Mental Disease | title=Safety and Efficacy of Lysergic Acid Diethylamide-Assisted Psychotherapy for Anxiety Associated With Life-threatening Diseases | volume=202 | issue=7 | pages=513–520 | date= July 2014 | url=https://journals.lww.com/00005053-201407000-00001 | issn=0022-3018 | doi=10.1097/NMD.0000000000000113}}</ref> However, it can also occur to a lesser extent under the influence of [[entactogen|entactogens]], [[dissociative|dissociatives]],<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6" /><ref name=":7" /> and [[meditation]].</onlyinclude>

===Analysis===
The culturally dominant definition of catharsis, releasing the pressure of negative emotions, was popularized by both Josef Breuer and Sigmund Freud as the hydraulic model in psychoanalysis<ref name=":0">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Bushman, B. J.)) | journal=Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin | title=Does Venting Anger Feed or Extinguish the Flame? Catharsis, Rumination, Distraction, Anger, and Aggressive Responding | volume=28 | issue=6 | pages=724–731 | date= June 2002 | url=http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0146167202289002 | issn=0146-1672 | doi=10.1177/0146167202289002}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Bohart, A. C.)) | journal=Psychotherapy: Theory, Research & Practice | title=Toward a cognitive theory of catharsis. | volume=17 | issue=2 | pages=192–201 | date= 1980 | url=http://doi.apa.org/getdoi.cfm?doi=10.1037/h0085911 | issn=0033-3204 | doi=10.1037/h0085911}}</ref> and Jakob Bernays's purgation theory in philology.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Golden, L.)) | journal=The Journal of Aesthetics and Art Criticism | title=The Purgation Theory of Catharsis | volume=31 | issue=4 | pages=473 | date= 1973 | url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/10.2307/429320?origin=crossref | issn=00218529 | doi=10.2307/429320}}</ref><ref>{{cite book | vauthors=((Porter, J. I.)) | veditors=((Billings, J.)), ((Leonard, M.)) | date=1 June 2015 | chapter=Tragedy and the Idea of Modernity | title=Jacob Bernays and the Catharsis of Modernity | publisher=Oxford University Press | pages=14–41 | url=https://oxford.universitypressscholarship.com/view/10.1093/acprof:oso/9780198727798.001.0001/acprof-9780198727798-chapter-2 | doi=10.1093/acprof:oso/9780198727798.003.0002 | isbn=9780198727798}}</ref> There is a large amount of discussion of these theories' unsuitability towards the emotion of anger, showing that acting aggressively produces more aggression.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Bushman, B. J.)), ((Baumeister, R. F.)), ((Stack, A. D.)) | journal=Journal of Personality and Social Psychology | title=Catharsis, aggression, and persuasive influence: Self-fulfilling or self-defeating prophecies? | volume=76 | issue=3 | pages=367–376 | date= 1999 | url=http://doi.apa.org/getdoi.cfm?doi=10.1037/0022-3514.76.3.367 | issn=1939-1315 | doi=10.1037/0022-3514.76.3.367}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Bushman, B. J.)), ((Baumeister, R. F.)), ((Phillips, C. M.)) | journal=Journal of Personality and Social Psychology | title=Do people aggress to improve their mood? Catharsis beliefs, affect regulation opportunity, and aggressive responding. | volume=81 | issue=1 | pages=17–32 | date= 2001 | url=http://doi.apa.org/getdoi.cfm?doi=10.1037/0022-3514.81.1.17 | issn=1939-1315 | doi=10.1037/0022-3514.81.1.17}}</ref> Aggression studies' applicability towards catharsis can be called into question though, specifically regarding the nature of security required to experience this effect.<ref>{{cite book | vauthors=((Geen, R. G.)), ((Quanty, M. B.)) | date= 1977 | chapter=Advances in Experimental Social Psychology | title=The Catharsis of Aggression: An Evaluation of a Hypothesis | publisher=Elsevier | volume=10 | pages=1–37 | url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0065260108603536 | doi=10.1016/S0065-2601(08)60353-6 | isbn=9780120152100}}</ref> It is also notable that Freud himself abandoned this model in practice, favouring the psychoanalytical technique of free association.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Nichols, M. P.)), ((Efran, J. S.)) | journal=Psychotherapy: Theory, Research, Practice, Training | title=Catharsis in psychotherapy: A new perspective. | volume=22 | issue=1 | pages=46–58 | date= 1985 | url=http://doi.apa.org/getdoi.cfm?doi=10.1037/h0088525 | issn=1939-1536 | doi=10.1037/h0088525}}</ref>
